sample_unit: model interactions (12 scenarios x 100 submissions x 2 tools)

links.outcome: Reproducibility of antibiotic recommendations across 100 repeated identical submissions
links.effect: Entropy ranged from 0 to 2.53; ChatGPT fully consistent in 5/12 cases vs 1/12 for OpenEvidence; probability two responses differed reached 81% in some scenarios.
links.quote: For antibiotic selection, entropy ranged from complete agreement (H = 0) to high heterogeneity (H up to 2.53).

links.outcome: Clinical correctness of antibiotic and duration recommendations rated by blinded infectious diseases specialists
links.effect: OpenEvidence correct antibiotic recommendations 54.8% vs ChatGPT 35.7% (P<0.001); fully correct combined responses 33.4% vs 19.0% (P<0.001).
links.quote: Despite lower reproducibility, OpenEvidence generated more correct antibiotic recommendations (54.8% vs 35.7%; P < 0.001) and more fully correct combined responses (33.4% vs 19.0%; P < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Evaluating reproducibility (output variability across identical repeated inputs) as a governance requirement alongside accuracy

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of the reproducibility and clinical correctness of LLM outputs (ChatGPT and OpenEvidence) across repeated identical prompts in standardized clinical scenarios.
